about: Figure-design principles from published guidance; every rule quotes its source verbatim (fetched 2026-11-13). Rougier et al. 2014 is CC0 (public domain).

rules.text: Decide who reads the figure and what it must convey before drawing — the Brief's takeaway and problem fields.

source.where: Rougier et al. 2014, Rule 1: Know Your Audience
source.quote: it is important to identify, as early as possible in the design process, the audience and the message the visual is to convey.

rules.text: One identified message steers every layout and emphasis choice; a figure without one becomes a parts list.

source.quote: Once clearly identified, this message will be a strong guide for the design of the figure

rules.text: Design for where the figure lives (single/double column, slide, poster) — print width and the font floor are part of the design, not an export detail.

source.where: Rule 3: Adapt the Figure to the Support Medium
source.quote: Ideally, each type of support medium requires a different figure

rules.text: The caption explains how to read the figure and holds what cannot be drawn; the main flow must still be readable without it.

source.quote: The caption explains how to read the figure and provides additional precision for what cannot be graphically represented.

rules.text: Tool defaults (one box style, one tint, a bottom legend) are good enough for any figure and best for none — choose every style deliberately.

source.where: Rule 5: Do Not Trust the Defaults
source.quote: In other words, they are good enough for any plot but they are best for none.

rules.text: Colour carries meaning (contribution, representation type); used without a plan it confuses — declare color_semantics.

source.quote: color can be either your greatest ally or your worst enemy if not used properly.

rules.text: Remove decoration that carries no information (containers around single items, gratuitous shadows/icons).

source.quote: Chartjunk refers to all the unnecessary or confusing visual elements found in a figure

rules.text: Readability and the message come first; beauty is pursued within them, never against them.

source.quote: Remember, in science, message and readability of the figure is the most important aspect while beauty is only an option

rules.text: Use one sans-serif typeface (Helvetica/Arial) for all figure text.

source.quote: All text should be a sans-serif typeface, preferably Helvetica or Arial.

rules.text: Nature prints figure text between 5 and 7 pt; the skill's 7 pt floor is stricter (conference columns are wider and read on screen).

source.quote: Maximum text size for all other text is 7-pt and the minimum is 5-pt.

rules.text: Use a colour-blind-accessible palette (Wong 2011 / Okabe–Ito); lint tone-confusable checks it.

source.quote: An accessible colour palette to be used (for example Wong, B. Points of view: Colour blindness. Nature Methods 8, 441 (2011).)

rules.text: Do not encode meaning with coloured text alone; use a key or a shape cue.

source.quote: Coloured text; keylines, keys, etc. should be used instead
